summary: Reproduced the DeepSeek-V4 encoder accepting a trailing system message and omitting the assistant generation prefix. The encoder now rejects system messages after the conversation has started; the OpenAI serving base maps this ValueError to HTTP 400 before inference. Valid leading-system and user-tail prompts retain their generation prefixes, and context plus new messages are validated as one conversation.

tests.what_was_measured: The reported system-tail prompt ended without <｜Assistant｜><think>, while changing only the tail role to user produced that prefix; raw output is in reproduction-before.log.
The issue-specific regression failed because the malformed ordering did not raise; the independent valid boundaries passed. Raw output is in regression-before.log.

The reported tool-calling sequence is rejected, valid leading-system and no-system prompts keep generation prefixes, and a system turn introduced after prior context is rejected. Raw output is in regression-after.log.
All 10 DeepSeek-V4-focused serving-chat unit tests passed; raw output is in dsv4-tests.log.
The system-tail case raises a precise ordering error at index 4 and the user-tail control still ends in <｜Assistant｜><think>; raw output is in reproduction-after.log.
The changed encoder and retained reproduction script compile successfully.

gpu_execution.evidence: This defect is deterministic prompt construction and rejection before tokenization/model execution. No DeepSeek-V4 weights were available, and a tiny Llama transport fixture cannot qualify DeepSeek-V4 architecture behavior, semantic generation, or the reported long-context EOS outcome.

remaining_limitations: No DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 weights were available, so the reported 10/10 first-token EOS behavior was not replayed on a model.

No HTTP server with a DeepSeek-V4 tokenizer/model was launched. HTTP 400 mapping is established by the existing OpenAIServingBase.handle_request ValueError handling; the issue-specific tests exercise the actual custom encoder path.
GPU execution was not relevant to the pre-inference message-order validation and was not used.
The prepared environment does not include ruff; git diff --check and Python compilation succeeded instead.
